Hi Samantha — attaching a simplified excerpted diagram (edge_fence_diagram.png) and a brief note below to complement Jordan's playbook.

Key points (short):
- Dedicated deployment model: customer traffic terminates at a VPC peering endpoint or private connect. From there, egress is strictly controlled — no direct public IPs on inference hosts.
- Control plane (management API, model registry) runs in a logically separated control VPC. All control plane calls are authenticated with mTLS and RBAC; data-plane requests never carry tenant plaintext keys.
- Cryptographic boundaries: tenant encryption keys are stored in the customer's KMS when requested; Redwood's runtime only receives key-wrapping tokens. For customers opting in to HSM-backed KMS, we produce an audit trail of the unwrap operations mapped to request IDs.
- KV cache and prompt prefixes are namespace-isolated per customer. Memory-level isolation is enforced in the runtime and backed by nightly process attestation.

Attached exhibits: edge_fence_diagram.png (for SIG reviewers) and the playbook PDF already shared. Happy to expand any section for the walkthrough.

--

Samantha — attaching SIG mapping (sig_mapping_v1.csv) that maps the BlueBank question rows to our artifacts and evidence pockets. A few notes inline:

- Network isolation (SIG.SC-2 / CAIQ:Network): annotated in column C -> diagram page 2. The "Dedicated GPU pool" is modeled as a tenant-isolated compute cluster with per-tenant ACLs enforced at the hypervisor/namespace level.
- Control-plane leakage risk: we've documented fallback routing and a hardened proxy that only permits selected control-plane RPCs; see mitigation notes (row 17).
- Egress and telemetry: default is deny-all with allowlists; telemetry endpoints are signed and only reachable via a restricted NAT gateway.

Walkthrough: Thu 07/09 11:00 PST works for us — we'll be prepared to show the diagram and live-map a request flow. Please share the attendee list and any additional items you want us to cover.
